question: Does a visually fast,large-amplitude,multi-phase real action sequence reveal failures not observed in the prior low-density pilot?

action_sequence.observation: Standing cross-step, arms open, torso lowers toward the first hand plant.
First large hand-supported circular leg sweep: torso tips forward on the hands, legs swing behind and then open into a large elevated split in front before rotating back down.
Second successive hand-supported circular leg-sweep cycle, again passing from face-down support through a large high/low leg split before returning low.
Low supported sweeping pivot; leg comes around and feet gather to end the floor sequence.
Hands leave the ground, feet widen and torso rises from the floor sequence into upright stance.
One small upright two-foot hop, followed by landing; this is distinct from the earlier hand-supported airborne leg motions.
Landed upright finishing adjustment with back toward camera.

arms.a: recolor shirt and general motion preservation
arms.b: same edit plus explicit original action sequence,count and approximate timing

pairing: same actual AV initial noise,source/dense reference,reference augmentation seed and sampler within each A/B pair
preconditions: Readmission on free A10080GB and isolated newbase
Same-shape2step benchmark validates runtime speed; not a formal result
Inspect actual prepared reference and VAE reconstruction for all action phases before interpreting downstream failures
evaluation: Check ordering and source-frame timing of short exit/rise/landing transitions
Distinguish visual degradation,hand/foot topology/contact errors from event omission
No time warping or interpolated quality scoring; allframes/1x/quarter-speed review
inference_limits: One new source; not a controlled causal manipulation of motion density,amplitude or transition speed
Source contains2repeated sweep cycles plus distinct entry/exit/rise/hop phases,not many unrelated tricks
Original capture/author slow-motion cannot be certified; no added speed changes and observed source playback is fast
Expected2fps does not directly observe every transitional pose; this alone is not evidence of a pathway conflict
Explicit prompt is a privileged simple baseline,not an automatic method
